what: A CHERRY-PICK CAN PERMANENTLY ADMIT A LANE SESSION TO THE MANAGER ROSTER, AFTER WHICH ITS ORDINARY WORK READS AS VIOLATIONS. Found the hard way, and three separate remedies failed before the cause was understood. MECHANISM, quoted from the guard's own output: `dispatch observations derived from 674 revision(s) of docs/claude/work/MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json (population: EVERY REVISION REACHABLE FROM --all)`. Roster membership is therefore GLOBAL to the repository, while violations are per-commit-in-range. A cherry-pick RE-PARENTS a commit and so changes its DIFF: a lane's ordinary checklist edit, re-parented, reads as newly setting other rows' `lane` — a dispatch act. MEASURED on the two branches: old branch `13 act(s) ... by 1 session(s)`, roster 8; rebuilt branch `15 act(s) ... by 2 session(s)`, roster 9. The added session is the E43 LANE, which never dispatched anything. [!] ADMISSION IS PERMANENT AND UNDOABLE FROM A BRANCH. Once admitted, every commit that session authors in any range is graded under manager rules, on any branch, forever — so its writing scripts/ops/** and tests/** (its actual job) grades as `a manager session doing an item`. [!] THREE REMEDIES FAILED FOR ONE REASON, and the reason is the finding: the guard grades an ACT THAT ALREADY EXISTS, and no later act removes it. (1) The manager's revert+reapply of its own commit — failed, and would have 'succeeded' only by widening the UNGRADED set, which is green-while-measuring-nothing. (2) Deleting the stale merge-slot claim — tested by the lane, all findings intact. (3) Stripping every docs/claude/work/** edit off the code branch, leaving only the tooling and tests — tested by the lane on a branch cut from current main, STILL `violation`, because the admitting revisions live on other branches entirely. [!] THE HONEST DISPOSITION TAKEN: PR #12759 is left UNLANDED with the red guard visible rather than landed behind a manager-scope exception. The exception was the lane's own recommendation and was declined, by both of us in the end, on the grounds that an exception records a defect as handled and leaves it. ⚠️ Note also that the manager COULD NOT have written that exception: the runtime classifier refused it as [Self-Modification], and having the lane write it on the manager's word would have routed around that refusal. [!] COST OF LEAVING IT: scripts/ops/merge_json_register.py's `updated_by` fix is complete, tested 32/32, and OBSERVED resolving four real merges — and it does not reach main, so every lane keeps hand-resolving MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json. That is the bottleneck this row is paying to keep visible. [!] SAME CLASS AS THE DAY'S OTHER FINDINGS: an instrument answering correctly about a population that moved underneath it. This guard is one day old (#12740).
